Episode 134. Duel on the Ship (3)
Flash!
A dazzling light filled their vision first.
There was not a single person in the world who could react to the ultimate light-speed thrust by simply 'seeing' it.
One could only avoid it by predicting, or by achieving some sort of realization beyond even that.

Fortunately, Mary's fifth secret technique had not yet reached its peak. In addition, because she had unleashed it so quickly without any preparation, Jin was able to move his body despite being off-guard.
He threw himself to the left.
The attack range of the light-speed thrust was not limited to a single point. It started at a point, spread out in a fan shape, and then converged back to a point.
As a result, Jin had to feel the sword energy brushing past his cheeks and neck, even though he had moved far away from the trajectory of the chained sword, Doksa.
He felt a chill down his spine.
'Is Tikan okay?'
As the sensation of hot blood soaking his collar flowed, Jin quickly calculated in his head how to deal with the situation.
'Don't look back, counterattack first.'
He judged that the direction of the light-speed thrust narrowly missed Tikan.
After all, his sister wouldn't have defied their father's orders and unleashed the light-speed thrust, knowing that she would become an enemy of both him and Cheolcheon Jiwonsu.
Crash-!

Jin, crouching low, lunged forward like an arrow and swung his sword. The first sword he chose was the Bongroe Sword Sigmund, and its pale and sharp lightning energy reached out towards Mary's forehead.
She easily blocked her brother's thrust. Then, she let out a hearty laugh, seemingly very satisfied.
The ensuing exchange between the siblings was fast and dizzying, with two streaks of light reflecting and intertwining.
The audience couldn't even follow the movements of the swords that flashed, scattered, and reattached.
"Whoa! Mary is showing something amazing from the first move! Eek! What is that, what is that! There's a hole in the sky above Tikan!"
Cosmos seemed to be not only the referee but also the commentator for the match.
The audience followed his finger and looked up at the sky, and indeed, they saw a giant hole pierced through the clouds and let out a sigh.
It was hard to believe that a human could create such a phenomenon with just a single swing of a sword.
Is this Runcandel...?
Everyone couldn't help but admire it. Of course, Mary's near-miraculous thrust, but also Jin, who had managed to dodge and counterattack in the midst of it, looked like a monster.
Not only the crowd but also Jin's teammates were shivering at Mary's skills and sticking their tongues out.
"A thrust like that from a standstill. No, can that even be called a thrust? Now I understand why Valkas told us to bet on Mary."
At Kashimir's words, Valkas quietly smiled.
"Seeing Cosmos babble on unharmed, it seems that Tikan didn't take any damage."
Jin inwardly patted himself on the chest, realizing that his immediate counterattack was the perfect response.
If he had hesitated even a little or tried to check on Tikan first, he would have had to deal with a follow-up attack in a broken stance.
"Damn, it seems I still can't measure up to Father. I practiced quite a bit too."
Seeing his sister's discontent as she spoke, his anger boiled up, but he barely managed to suppress it and met her gaze.
"It seems you came with the intention to kill me. My head almost disappeared."
"You didn't die, did you? I knew you would react, hehe."
"...Didn't you say we should avoid big moves first?"
"Hehe, me? When?"
"No, surely."
"Really, if you think so, recall what I said, little brother."
-The rules are simple. You and I will fight on the fleet. However, high-destruction moves that would excessively damage the fleet are all prohibited.
-Although we agreed to seal most of our big moves in this duel, I will still do my best.
Prohibiting moves that would excessively damage the fleet, sealing most big moves, but still doing one's best...
In other words, as long as the move didn't destroy the fleet, it didn't matter what kind of move was used.
'Was it wordplay?'
He unintentionally gritted his teeth.
Come to think of it, their first duel was the same.
At that time, too, Mary fought wearing only her own silver armor, laying down top-tier magic bombs all around.
Jin rarely fell for wordplay or shallow tricks, but strangely, whenever he faced Mary, he always found himself being tricked in this manner.
"I understand what you mean."
"Really? I'm so relieved you finally understand. Now come on, attack me again! But why didn't you activate your helmet?"
With an agitated voice, Mary pointed at Jin's head with the tip of her sword.
"Ah, are you talking about Muta's rune?"
"Is that what it's called? Anyway, that black helmet. If you had used it, you wouldn't have been hurt like this."
"It's for the same reason you're wearing an eyepatch."
Mary hesitated at Jin's response.
She didn't wear an eyepatch because she lost her sight. She thought that if Jin couldn't use his magic sword techniques or Myungwang Army tactics, then she could afford to have a handicap like this.
Mary believed that Jin was clearly superior to her, but at least in terms of pure swordsmanship, she had faith that she was ahead.
"Oh, really?"
"Think about it, sister. Our first duel was evenly matched. Even then, I was scared that you might die, so I held back. But do I need to use such an artifact?"
"You can say that after I take off my eyepatch, little brother!"
As soon as she finished speaking, the distance closed again. In a blink, the poisonous snake had flown right in front of his nose, blocking his vision.
As he lifted his sword to deflect what he thought was a thrust, the chain sword unraveled and changed its path.
The chain sword, moving like a snake or a whip, attacked from all directions, making it hard to believe it was just one person's offensive.
To the spectators, it seemed as if Jin was completely trapped within the trajectories and afterimages of the chain sword. With each step, the wooden deck cracked and splinters flew.
The pressure of the chain sword was getting heavier.
It was the result of Mary's body being imbued with aura. It was a technique that could be called physical enhancement rather than the self-destructive mode of the 7th Final Weapon.
Runcandel's 7th Final Weapon
Volcano - Mary Runcandel
The reason Mary named it Volcano was that Chiron personally allowed her to do so.
Jin had seen Mary's Volcano in action only once before. It was a little different in shape now than it was then.
'It's a variation of the Volcano she used when she saved the small creatures from the Ghost Road. I wonder if it's advanced or just a different feeling.'
There was no time to reminisce with gratitude.
There was also no need to ask if it was okay to use such a powerful sword that could destroy the entire fleet.
Cough-!
As soon as the Volcano was activated and the swords clashed, Jin spat blood and stepped back.
It was a strange sword.
Mary's sword strike with the Volcano activated was worthy of being called the sincere strike of a 10-star martial artist, yet for some reason, it didn't inflict any damage on anything other than Jin.
'...The shock doesn't escape outside?'
Mary's poisonous snake with the Volcano activated only affected Jin.
Even when Jin was struck with a force strong enough to make him vomit blood, not even a small crack appeared on the deck.

That's why it looked like the siblings were playing from the outside. With just ordinary offense and defense going on, Jin was the only one twisting his body or vomiting blood whenever the sword touched him.
As the shock that should naturally escape outward was only swirling within his body, it was an incredibly difficult phenomenon for Jin to accept.
"Ah, what's going on here! It looks like a light attack, but Jin is vomiting blood profusely! It's a crisis for Jin!"
Like the audience, most of Tikan's companions couldn't understand the spectacle either. It was a type of sword even Kashimir, known as the legendary sword, had never seen before.

"Indeed, Valkas, your assessment of her wasn't entirely wrong. I never thought Mary Runcandel would have reached that level already. She seems to have a more delicate side than I thought? There weren't many people who used that in my time."
Murakan, who had lived for over three thousand years and had been with the Roon Candles in their prime, recognized the level she had reached right away.
"What is happening?"
"Well, uh, Quicantel. What was it called again? It's been so long since I've seen it that I can't remember."
"Témar called it Passionate Heart 熱心. It was mainly used by fighters rather than swordsmen."

"Ah, that's right. The Passionate Sword, that was the name. It's a sword that causes internal damage without any external impact. That's why the little guy is in pain from what looks like an ordinary attack."
Cough, cough, cough!
With each touch of the sword, a terrible pain as if dozens of awls were tearing through his organs came. Cold sweat filled the spaces between his standing hairs.
First, he had to create distance.
Jin knew that was the obvious response. However, he couldn't use a technique powerful enough to push Mary away, and with limited space, it wasn't easy.
'...Mary can't keep using this sword while maintaining the Volcano. The Volcano's transformation itself is a technique that puts a tremendous strain on the body.'
But relying solely on that and trying to buy time was a gamble and an impossible task. The magic spells, including the lightning cannon, couldn't buy him time since Mary already had the information.
So, he had to finish it in one go.
And in fact, Jin had planned to do so from the beginning. He was just a little taken aback by the variables of the light-speed thrust and the Passionate Sword.
Despite knowing that it wasn't suitable for battle under such limited conditions, there was a reason why he chose the Myeongwang Sword 'first.'
As soon as the energy from the Myeongwang Sword quickly spread through Jin's body, Mary opened her mouth.
"Is it that technique you showed in the Sword Garden? That will surely disqualify you. Or do you want to kill me regardless of the outcome?"
As Jin nodded, Mary let out a faint laugh.
